newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey still trying to sell sugar to Iran.
newsitem.headline: Turkey still trying to sell sugar to Iran.

text.p: Turkey was still negotiating with Iran to sell it at least 50,000 tonnes of white sugar agreed last month in Ankara, Selahattin Hun, general manager of the state sugar refineries Turkseker, said on Thursday.
"We are still holding talks with Iranians. We are negotiating over the price," Hun told Reuters.
Turkey agreed with Iran in December to sell it 50,000 tonnes of sugar and later said the amount could be raised if necessary.
Hun did not say when the negotiations could end.
He said the sales to Iran would be made through a tender to local firms which will later sell the sugar to Iran. He did not give other details.
Turkey said last month it was told by a senior delegation who visited Ankara in December that Iran needed to buy about 600,000 tonnes of sugar this year, some of which could come from Turkey.

Turkey, after being a net sugar importer for the past two years, began exporting from its expected output of about 1.85 million tonnes in 1996/97, up from 1.5 million tonnes a year earlier. --Ercan Ersoy, Ankara Newsroom, 90-312-4462940
